chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from 'Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever neglects throwing the Jamarat or some of them until the days of Tashreeq have passed, he must throw them the following year. If he does not perform Hajj, his Wali (guardian) should throw on his behalf. If he has no Wali, he should seek help from a Muslim man to throw on his behalf, for the throwing of the Jamarat occurs only during the days of Tashreeq."
And it has been narrated that whoever deliberately leaves throwing the Jamarat, women are not permissible to him, and he must perform Hajj the following year. This was narrated.

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for missing the Jamarat throwing during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the fiqh of missed Jamarat throwing, emphasizing that the specific window for this act is limited to the Days of Tashreeq, with missed obligations deferred to the following year. It distinguishes between accidental omission and deliberate neglect, the latter carrying the severe penalty of 'holding back' (imprisonment or restriction) and requiring a make-up Hajj, a ruling often linked to the concept of *Habs* in Shia jurisprudence. The inclusion of a guardian (*wali*) or a substitute Muslim highlights the communal responsibility in ensuring the completion of Hajj pillars.
